- Carbohydrate distribution: spread carbs evenly across meals (rather than one large carb meal) to blunt post‑prandial peaks.

- Use new 1RM values to set future training percentages and progression (e.g., 70–85% 1RM for strength blocks).

Sample Week 7 (intensified)
- Mon: Strength A — Back squat 5 x 4–5, RDL 4 x 5, Bench 4 x 5, Rows 3 x 6–8
- Tue: HIIT 9 x 20s/80s or 6 x 30s/90s
- Wed: Hypertrophy/power — swings, Bulgarian, press, pull-ups, superset finisher
- Thu: Active recovery 25–30 min easy
- Fri: Strength C — Deadlift 5 x 3, Front squat 4 x 6, Incline press 3 x 6–8
- Sat: Tempo 30–35 min RPE 6–7
- Sun: Rest

PHASE 3 — STRENGTH & CONSOLIDATION (Weeks 9–12) — 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-23
Goals: Heavier lifts with preserved hypertrophy volume, consolidate gains, keep cardio for caloric expenditure and aerobic capacity, conduct safe taper and 1RM test late in Week 12 (if prerequisites met).

Key features:
- Two strength-focused sessions (heavier, low reps) and one hypertrophy/power session per week.
- Cardio: keep one HIIT limited (Phase 2 HIIT can reduce here to once every 7–10 days) and maintain tempo/long session; prioritize recovery.
- Week 11: maintain intensity; Week 12: taper (reduce volume ~25–35%, maintain some heavy singles for readiness), then test 1RM on selected lifts under safe protocol.
- If client shows any red flags, postpone 1RM testing and use submaximal alternatives.

Weeks 9–10 (2026-07-27 to 2026-08-09)
Weekly template
- Mon: Resistance A — Strength (Squat heavy)
- Tue: Zone 2 steady 35–45 min or optional short HIIT every 10 days
- Wed: Resistance B — Hypertrophy/power
- Thu: Active recovery or mobility / light cardio
- Fri: Resistance C — Strength (Deadlift heavy)
- Sat: Long low-intensity cardio 45–60 min (Zone 1–2)
- Sun: Rest

Sessions examples

Session A — Strength (Mon)
1. Warm-up
2. Back squat — 5 x 3–5 @ RPE 8–8.5 (2–3 min rest)
3. Romanian or stiff-leg deadlift — 3 x 6–8
4. Bench press or weighted dips — 4 x 4–6
5. Barbell row or chest-supported row — 3 x 6–8
6. Core 2–3 sets

Session B — Hypertrophy/power (Wed)
1. Warm-up
2. Kettlebell swings or jump variant (if safe) — 4 x 6–8
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10
4. Overhead press — 3 x 6–8
5. Pull-ups weighted or chin-ups — 3 x 5–8
6. Metabolic finisher (optional moderate): 12 min EMOM or 10–12 min AMRAP at moderate intensity

Session C — Strength (Fri)
1. Warm-up
2. Deadlift — 5 x 3–5 alternating conventional or trap bar across weeks @ RPE 8
3. Front squat — 4 x 6
4. Incline bench or close-grip bench — 3 x 6–8
5. Single-arm row — 3 x 8 each

Weeks 11–12 (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-23) — consolidate then taper/test
Week 11 (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-16): keep intensity similar to Weeks 9–10; reduce accessory volume by ~10–15% to fresher baseline for testing week.
Week 12 (2026-08-17 to 2026-08-23): Taper + 1RM testing
- Week 12 plan: Reduce total volume by ~25–35%; keep warm-up quality and perform heavier singles during warm-up but reduce accessory work. Ensure 48–72 hours between heavy testing of different lifts.
- Planned 1RM tests: choose up to two lifts (recommended: trap-bar deadlift and back squat OR one lower-body and one upper like bench if tested). Prefer trap-bar deadlift over conventional deadlift for lower injury risk if unfamiliar.
- Use the safe 1RM protocol below. If any recovery/nutrition/menstrual red flags present, do not test — instead perform 3RM or predicted 1RM tests.

1RM testing plan (Week 12) — safe protocol
Prerequisites 48–72 hours before test:
- Sleep 7+ hours/night for 2 nights
- Maintenance calorie intake for 48–72 hours prior; pre-test meal 60–90 minutes before with ~30–50 g carbs + ~20–30 g protein
- No HIIT within 48 hours prior
- RHR within normal range; no significant DOMS or injury
- Proper spotter/safety pins and coaching available

Warm-up & attempt progression (example for squat or trap bar)
- 8–10 min general warm-up (bike/row)
- Empty bar x 8–10
- 40% estimated 1RM x 5
- 60% x 3
- 75% x 2
- 85% x 1
- 92–95% x 1
- Rest 2–5 min then attempt heavier singles increasing by 1–5% depending on feel. Limit total maximal attempts to 3–6 including top attempts. Stop if technique breaks or sharp pain occurs.

Alternatives if test not advisable: 3RM or 5RM test and estimate 1RM using Epley/Brzycki equation.

Nutrition plan (rolled in with program) — glycaemic control + fueling for higher intensity

Overview targets
- Start conservative deficit −200 to −350 kcal/day (use cyclical deficit 3 weeks on / 1 week maintenance).
- Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day.
- Fat: ~25–30% of calories, focus on unsaturated fats and omega‑3s.
- Carbs: 35–45% of calories overall — concentrate carbs around sessions (pre/post).
- Fibre: ≥25–35 g/day.
- Hydration: 1.5–3 L/day depending on sweat and heat.
- Supplementation: vitamin D if deficient, creatine 3–5 g/day if cleared by clinician, omega‑3 1 g/day optional.

Daily meal timing & examples
- Meal pattern: 3 meals + 1–2 snacks. Aim for ~20–35 g protein per meal; distribute carbs around training.
- Pre-workout (if session >30–40 min or high intensity): 30–60 g carbs + 15–25 g protein 60–90 minutes before.
- Post-workout: 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein within 60–90 minutes.
- Higher-intensity days (HIIT, strength days): increase carbs by ~25–40 g versus rest days; avoid aggressive carb cuts on heavy days.
- Evening meals: prioritise protein and veg; moderate carb portion.

Sample daily (training day, ~1750–1850 kcal moderate deficit)
- Breakfast: Porridge (40 g oats), 150 g Greek yoghurt, 50–60 g berries, 1 tbsp nuts — ~30 g protein
- Snack/pre-workout: Banana + 15 g whey — 20–30 g carbs, 15 g protein
- Lunch: 120 g grilled chicken, 1/2 cup cooked quinoa, large salad w/ olive oil — ~35 g protein
- Post-workout snack: Smoothie: 1 scoop whey, 150 ml milk, handful spinach — 20–25 g protein
- Dinner: 120 g salmon, 150 g sweet potato, steamed veg — ~30 g protein
- Optional small cottage cheese snack if needed — +7–10 g protein

Carb cycling & refeeds
- Use maintenance week every 3 weeks: eat to maintenance calories and slightly raise carbs across the day to support hormones and training.
- Short tighter blocks (7–10 days) of larger deficits (−450 to −500 kcal/day) are allowed only rarely and with protections: no HIIT, reduced cardio, increased protein, strict monitoring and clinician awareness.

Cardio additions (rolled in)
Phase 1: 2 low-intensity/week (Tue, Sat)
Phase 2: Tue HIIT (short) + Sat tempo; Thu optional light recovery; optional 2nd HIIT only with monitoring
Phase 3: maintain tempo/long sessions; limit HIIT (every 7–10 days) and prioritize recovery before 1RM testing

HIIT protocols (short, safe examples)
- Option A: 8–10 x 20s all-out / 80–100s easy (bike/row/assault)
- Option B: 6–8 x 30s hard / 90s easy
- Keep total session 15–25 min. Pre-check: sleep, RHR, appetite, soreness all OK before attempting HIIT.

Autoregulation & monitoring (daily/weekly)
Daily quick check (client completes each morning)
- Sleep hours last night (target 7–9)
- Resting HR (compare to baseline)
- Energy / mood scale 1–10
- Any menstrual bleeding or changes
- Soreness scale and appetite
If RHR > +7–10 bpm above baseline for 48 hours or sleep <6 hrs x2, reduce training intensity that day: no HIIT, replace tempo with LISS, increase calories by ~250–400 kcal/day, and consider an extra rest day.

Weekly coach check (10–15 min)
- Review weights used, RPE, steps, sleep, menstrual notes, appetite, bodyweight trend (1x/week).
- Adjust loads, cardio volume, or calories accordingly. If menstrual cycles lengthen or amenorrhea increases, prioritize raising energy availability and reducing cardio before reducing resistance training.

Progression & loading rules (how to increase weight)
- Major lifts: increase load by 2.5–5% when top of rep range completed across all sets at RPE ≤8 and form is good.
- Accessory lifts: increase reps or add a set before increasing load.
- Use RPE as primary autoregulator. Stop 1–2 reps short of failure for heavy work. Use AMRAPs/some drop sets sparingly (Phase 2 occasional).

Deloads & planned recovery
- Built-in micro-deload in Week 8 if signs of fatigue: reduce volume by 20–30% (drop accessory sets, reduce HIIT to steady-state).
- Week 12 is a taper for testing: reduce volume 25–35% while keeping intensity on singles.
- After the 12‑week cycle, plan 1 week of easier activity or a deload before starting the next block.

Injury prevention & technique notes
- Prioritise technique coaching for barbell lifts; regress to DB/KB variations if mobility or control is insufficient.
- Use full warm-ups and movement prep for squats/deadlifts; progress hinge pattern carefully.
- If any joint pain occurs: reduce ROM, reduce load, or replace with a pain-free substitute (e.g., trap-bar for conventional deadlift).

End-of-programme assessment (Week 12 & post-program)
- Strength: 1RM test if safe or 3–5RM predicted 1RM if not safe.
- Body composition: monthly photos, circumference measurements and bodyweight trend (not daily weigh-ins).
- Labs: coordinate with endocrinologist for HbA1c re-check at >3 months if clinically indicated.
- Menstrual function: review cycle tracking; if worsened, prioritize nutritional adjustments and physician review.

Practical deliverables I can produce next
- Printable calendar with each day’s session filled in and dates.
- Spreadsheet to track loads, RPE, steps, sleep, and menstrual notes.
- Exact calorie/macro numbers tailored to her current bodyweight and activity level.
- Meal plan templates for heavy training days vs rest days.

Below is the complete 12‑week programme starting 2026‑06‑01, with all adjustments you asked for rolled in: resistance training (priority for insulin sensitivity), progressive phases, intensified Phase 2 with higher intensity and two HIIT options (kept conservative), added cardio, a glycaemic‑focused nutrition plan with fueling for higher output, a cautious approach to calorie reductions (cyclical mild deficit), autoregulation/red‑flag rules, and a safe 1RM testing plan at the end of Phase 3. I’ve included specific session plans (exercises, sets/reps, tempo), weekly schedules with dates, nutrition guidelines for training vs rest days, monitoring checks, and the 1RM testing protocol. Use this as the working programme you deliver to the client; adjust loads individually using RPE and observed technique.

Important preface / safety rules (read before starting)
- Ensure initial baseline screening and movement check (squat, hinge, push, pull, single‑leg) before week 1. Use regressions if movement is poor.
- Resistances start at weights that produce RPE 6–7 for top prescribed reps. Increase only when form is solid and RPE ≤8.
- Protein: aim 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day. Initial calorie approach: conservative deficit −200 to −350 kcal/day (use maintenance if not provided). Use cyclical deficit: 3 weeks mild deficit, 1 week maintenance (or 2:1 weeks).
- HIIT frequency: generally 1 HIIT/week (Tuesday); Phase 2 allows up to 2 HIITs/week only with strict safeguards and monitoring and only short low‑volume protocols. If client requests daily HIIT, decline; do not program daily HIIT.
- Autoregulation: track resting HR, sleep, mood, appetite, training performance and menstrual notes. If any red flags (resting HR +7–10 bpm above baseline for 48 hours, sleep <6 hrs x2 nights, major performance drop, menstrual worsening, persistent low mood/appetite), reduce cardio first, increase calories ~250–400 kcal/day and/or cut HIIT. Prioritise recovery.
- Equipment assumed available: barbell + rack, trap bar or kettlebells, dumbbells, cable or band options, bench, rower/bike/assault bike optional.

Calendar overview (dates)
- Phase 1 Adaptation: Weeks 1–4 — 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-28
- Phase 2 Build (intensified): Weeks 5–8 — 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-26
- Phase 3 Strength & Consolidation: Weeks 9–12 — 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-23
- 1RM testing planned in Week 12 after a light taper the week prior.

Weekly template (general)
- Monday: Resistance Session A (strength or squat focus depending on phase)
- Tuesday: Cardio — typically HIIT (short) or Zone 2 depending on phase & recovery
- Wednesday: Resistance Session B (hypertrophy/power or hinge focus)
- Thursday: Active recovery / optional light cardio or mobility
- Friday: Resistance Session C (strength/hybrid)
- Saturday: Longer steady-state / tempo cardio (duration varies by phase)
- Sunday: Rest / mobility

Detailed week‑by‑week plan

PHASE 1 — ADAPTATION (Weeks 1–4) — 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-28
Goals: Technique, baseline strength, build aerobic base with low recovery cost, establish nutrition and monitoring routine.

General cardio in Phase 1: 2 lower-intensity sessions/week
- Tuesday: 20–30 min brisk walk or easy bike (Zone 1–2)
- Saturday: 30–40 min easy long walk/bike (Zone 1)
Nutrition: Start mild deficit −200 to −300 kcal/day if weight loss is desired. Protein 1.6 g/kg/day. Carbs moderate and focused around training.

Weeks 1–2 (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-14) — foundational sessions (3x/week resistance)
Session structure: Warm-up 8–10 min; main lifts; accessories; mobility; ~45–60 min total.

Week 1 & 2 Sessions (A/B/C)
Session A — Squat emphasis (Mon)
1. Warm-up: 5–8 min bike + thoracic/hip mobility
2. Goblet squat — 3 x 10–12, tempo 2:0:1, RPE 6–7
3. Romanian deadlift (DB) — 3 x 10
4. Dumbbell bench press — 3 x 10–12
5. One‑arm DB row — 3 x 10 each
6. Pallof press (band/cable) — 2 x 12 each
7. Glute bridge — 2 x 12–15
8. Cooldown mobility 5–8 min

Session B — Hinge/posterior (Wed)
1. Warm-up
2. Trap-bar or kettlebell deadlift — 3 x 8–10
3. Reverse lunge — 3 x 8 each
4. Seated cable row or chest-supported row — 3 x 10–12
5. Overhead press (DB/bar) — 3 x 8–10
6. Lateral band walk or clamshells — 2 x 15
7. Bird-dog or dead-bug — 2 x 10 each

Session C — Push/Pull balance (Fri)
1. Warm-up
2. Front squat or goblet — 3 x 8–10
3. Kettlebell swing — 3 x 12–15 (power, controlled)
4. Incline DB press — 3 x 10–12
5. Assisted pull-up / lat pulldown — 3 x 6–10
6. Farmer carry — 2 x 30–45s
7. Core/mobility

Week 3–4 (2026-06-15 to 2026-06-28) — increase volume slightly
Progression: add 1 set to main compounds (so many become 4 sets), or increase weight to maintain RPE 7–8.
- Add one low metabolic finisher once per week if energy allows (5–8 min steady row/bike).
- Cardio unchanged: Tue 25–30 min walk; Sat 35–45 min easy.

PHASE 2 — BUILD & INTENSIFY (Weeks 5–8) — 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-26
Goals: Increase strength stimulus, hypertrophy, introduce low‑volume HIIT, raise cardio intensity, increase fueling around workouts. Monitor recovery closely. This phase is intensified as requested.

Key changes:
- Resistance: two sessions per week bias toward heavier strength (lower reps), one session hypertrophy/power with short rests/AMRAPs.
- Cardio: Tuesday = HIIT (short) each week; Saturday = tempo/threshold session; Thursday optional light recovery.
- Nutrition: increase carbs on training/HIIT days; keep protein 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day. Maintain cyclical deficit (3:1 weeks) and be ready to move to maintenance if recovery or menstrual function worsens.
- HIIT cap: 1 weekly HIIT standard. Up to 2 HIIT/week allowed only if monitoring clear (sleep, RHR, mood good) and HIITs are short and not on heavy lower-body lift days. For safety, we’ll program 1 HIIT and provide an optional 2nd HIIT template with strict pre-checks.

Weeks 5–6 (2026-06-29 to 2026-07-12) — introduce heavier loads and first HIIT
Weekly schedule (example)
- Mon (A): Strength focus
- Tue: HIIT short (see below)
- Wed (B): Hypertrophy/power
- Thu: Active recovery or 20–30 min easy
- Fri (C): Strength + accessory
- Sat: Tempo steady-state 35–45 min
- Sun: Rest

Session A — Strength focus (Mon)
1. Warm-up 8–10 min + barbell warm sets
2. Back squat (or front if mobility limited) — 4–5 x 5–6 (Week 5 start 4x6, Week 6 progress to 5x5), RPE 7.5–8.5
3. Romanian deadlift or trap bar — 4 x 6–8
4. Barbell bench press — 4 x 5–6
5. Bent-over row — 3 x 8
6. Pallof press — 3 x 10 each

Session B — Hypertrophy/power (Wed)
1. Warm-up
2. Kettlebell swings (power) — 4 x 8–10
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10 each
4. Overhead press — 3 x 8–10
5. Pull‑up/chin-up progression — 3 x 6–8
6. Superset finisher (2 rounds): DB incline press 10–12 + single-arm row 10–12
7. Core 2–3 sets

Session C — Strength + intensity (Fri)
1. Warm-up
2. Deadlift (trap bar or conventional, alternate intensity with squats across weeks) — 5 x 3–5 @ RPE ~8
3. Front squat or heavy goblet — 4 x 6–8
4. Incline or close-grip bench — 3 x 6–8
5. Single-arm row — 3 x 8 each
6. AMRAP 8 min (optional once/week): 10 swings + 8 lunges + 6 push-ups (moderate load)

Cardio Week 5–6 specifics
- Tue HIIT (example): 8 x 20s hard / 80s easy on bike or row; total 18–22 min incl. warm-up/cool-down.
- Sat Tempo: 25–30 min at RPE 6–7 plus warm-up/cool-down (~40–45 min total).
- Thu optional: 20–30 min easy walk/bike + mobility.

Nutrition adjustments (Phase 2)
- Training day carbs: 40–60 g pre-workout if session >45 min or high intensity; 20–40 g post-workout + 20–30 g protein.
- Maintain daily protein 1.6–1.8 g/kg.
- Keep deficit conservative: −200 to −350 kcal/day. If adding HIIT and tempo increases TDEE, prefer to let activity create additional deficit rather than deepening cut; increase calories if recovery suffers.

Weeks 7–8 (2026-07-13 to 2026-07-26) — push intensity, controlled progression
- Progression: increase load by 2.5–5% on main lifts when top sets achieved at RPE ≤8; increase HIIT reps slightly in Week 7 (e.g., 9 x 20s/80s) or slightly increase tempo duration; Week 8 is a micro deload if signs of fatigue appear (reduce volume ~20–30% and swap HIIT for moderate intervals or steady-state).
- Cardio same structure; optional second HIIT only with green-light monitoring (sleep, RHR, energy).

Sample Week 7 (intensified)
- Mon: Strength A — Back squat 5 x 4–5, RDL 4 x 5, Bench 4 x 5, Rows 3 x 6–8
- Tue: HIIT 9 x 20s/80s or 6 x 30s/90s
- Wed: Hypertrophy/power — swings, Bulgarian, press, pull-ups, superset finisher
- Thu: Active recovery 25–30 min easy
- Fri: Strength C — Deadlift 5 x 3, Front squat 4 x 6, Incline press 3 x 6–8
- Sat: Tempo 30–35 min RPE 6–7
- Sun: Rest

PHASE 3 — STRENGTH & CONSOLIDATION (Weeks 9–12) — 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-23
Goals: Heavier lifts with preserved hypertrophy volume, consolidate gains, keep cardio for caloric expenditure and aerobic capacity, conduct safe taper and 1RM test late in Week 12 (if prerequisites met).

Key features:
- Two strength-focused sessions (heavier, low reps) and one hypertrophy/power session per week.
- Cardio: keep one HIIT limited (Phase 2 HIIT can reduce here to once every 7–10 days) and maintain tempo/long session; prioritize recovery.
- Week 11: maintain intensity; Week 12: taper (reduce volume ~25–35%, maintain some heavy singles for readiness), then test 1RM on selected lifts under safe protocol.
- If client shows any red flags, postpone 1RM testing and use submaximal alternatives.

Weeks 9–10 (2026-07-27 to 2026-08-09)
Weekly template
- Mon: Resistance A — Strength (Squat heavy)
- Tue: Zone 2 steady 35–45 min or optional short HIIT every 10 days
- Wed: Resistance B — Hypertrophy/power
- Thu: Active recovery or mobility / light cardio
- Fri: Resistance C — Strength (Deadlift heavy)
- Sat: Long low-intensity cardio 45–60 min (Zone 1–2)
- Sun: Rest

Sessions examples

Session A — Strength (Mon)
1. Warm-up
2. Back squat — 5 x 3–5 @ RPE 8–8.5 (2–3 min rest)
3. Romanian or stiff-leg deadlift — 3 x 6–8
4. Bench press or weighted dips — 4 x 4–6
5. Barbell row or chest-supported row — 3 x 6–8
6. Core 2–3 sets

Session B — Hypertrophy/power (Wed)
1. Warm-up
2. Kettlebell swings or jump variant (if safe) — 4 x 6–8
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10
4. Overhead press — 3 x 6–8
5. Pull-ups weighted or chin-ups — 3 x 5–8
6. Metabolic finisher (optional moderate): 12 min EMOM or 10–12 min AMRAP at moderate intensity

Session C — Strength (Fri)
1. Warm-up
2. Deadlift — 5 x 3–5 alternating conventional or trap bar across weeks @ RPE 8
3. Front squat — 4 x 6
4. Incline bench or close-grip bench — 3 x 6–8
5. Single-arm row — 3 x 8 each

Weeks 11–12 (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-23) — consolidate then taper/test
Week 11 (2026-08-10 to 2026-08-16): keep intensity similar to Weeks 9–10; reduce accessory volume by ~10–15% to fresher baseline for testing week.
Week 12 (2026-08-17 to 2026-08-23): Taper + 1RM testing
- Week 12 plan: Reduce total volume by ~25–35%; keep warm-up quality and perform heavier singles during warm-up but reduce accessory work. Ensure 48–72 hours between heavy testing of different lifts.
- Planned 1RM tests: choose up to two lifts (recommended: trap-bar deadlift and back squat OR one lower-body and one upper like bench if tested). Prefer trap-bar deadlift over conventional deadlift for lower injury risk if unfamiliar.
- Use the safe 1RM protocol below. If any recovery/nutrition/menstrual red flags present, do not test — instead perform 3RM or predicted 1RM tests.

1RM testing plan (Week 12) — safe protocol
Prerequisites 48–72 hours before test:
- Sleep 7+ hours/night for 2 nights
- Maintenance calorie intake for 48–72 hours prior; pre-test meal 60–90 minutes before with ~30–50 g carbs + ~20–30 g protein
- No HIIT within 48 hours prior
- RHR within normal range; no significant DOMS or injury
- Proper spotter/safety pins and coaching available

Warm-up & attempt progression (example for squat or trap bar)
- 8–10 min general warm-up (bike/row)
- Empty bar x 8–10
- 40% estimated 1RM x 5
- 60% x 3
- 75% x 2
- 85% x 1
- 92–95% x 1
- Rest 2–5 min then attempt heavier singles increasing by 1–5% depending on feel. Limit total maximal attempts to 3–6 including top attempts. Stop if technique breaks or sharp pain occurs.

Alternatives if test not advisable: 3RM or 5RM test and estimate 1RM using Epley/Brzycki equation.

Nutrition plan (rolled in with program) — glycaemic control + fueling for higher intensity

Overview targets
- Start conservative deficit −200 to −350 kcal/day (use cyclical deficit 3 weeks on / 1 week maintenance).
- Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day.
- Fat: ~25–30% of calories, focus on unsaturated fats and omega‑3s.
- Carbs: 35–45% of calories overall — concentrate carbs around sessions (pre/post).
- Fibre: ≥25–35 g/day.
- Hydration: 1.5–3 L/day depending on sweat and heat.
- Supplementation: vitamin D if deficient, creatine 3–5 g/day if cleared by clinician, omega‑3 1 g/day optional.

Daily meal timing & examples
- Meal pattern: 3 meals + 1–2 snacks. Aim for ~20–35 g protein per meal; distribute carbs around training.
- Pre-workout (if session >30–40 min or high intensity): 30–60 g carbs + 15–25 g protein 60–90 minutes before.
- Post-workout: 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein within 60–90 minutes.
- Higher-intensity days (HIIT, strength days): increase carbs by ~25–40 g versus rest days; avoid aggressive carb cuts on heavy days.
- Evening meals: prioritise protein and veg; moderate carb portion.

Sample daily (training day, ~1750–1850 kcal moderate deficit)
- Breakfast: Porridge (40 g oats), 150 g Greek yoghurt, 50–60 g berries, 1 tbsp nuts — ~30 g protein
- Snack/pre-workout: Banana + 15 g whey — 20–30 g carbs, 15 g protein
- Lunch: 120 g grilled chicken, 1/2 cup cooked quinoa, large salad w/ olive oil — ~35 g protein
- Post-workout snack: Smoothie: 1 scoop whey, 150 ml milk, handful spinach — 20–25 g protein
- Dinner: 120 g salmon, 150 g sweet potato, steamed veg — ~30 g protein
- Optional small cottage cheese snack if needed — +7–10 g protein

Carb cycling & refeeds
- Use maintenance week every 3 weeks: eat to maintenance calories and slightly raise carbs across the day to support hormones and training.
- Short tighter blocks (7–10 days) of larger deficits (−450 to −500 kcal/day) are allowed only rarely and with protections: no HIIT, reduced cardio, increased protein, strict monitoring and clinician awareness.

Cardio additions (rolled in)
Phase 1: 2 low-intensity/week (Tue, Sat)
Phase 2: Tue HIIT (short) + Sat tempo; Thu optional light recovery; optional 2nd HIIT only with monitoring
Phase 3: maintain tempo/long sessions; limit HIIT (every 7–10 days) and prioritize recovery before 1RM testing

HIIT protocols (short, safe examples)
- Option A: 8–10 x 20s all-out / 80–100s easy (bike/row/assault)
- Option B: 6–8 x 30s hard / 90s easy
- Keep total session 15–25 min. Pre-check: sleep, RHR, appetite, soreness all OK before attempting HIIT.

Autoregulation & monitoring (daily/weekly)
Daily quick check (client completes each morning)
- Sleep hours last night (target 7–9)
- Resting HR (compare to baseline)
- Energy / mood scale 1–10
